summary: Intermittent inference timeouts and p99 spikes traced to DNS-based egress failover causing cross-region hairpin
description:
Issue summary:

AuroraAnalytics reports intermittent request timeouts (HTTP 504) and elevated inference p99 latency for their dedicated capacity cluster in us-west. Incidents occur primarily during customer peak traffic windows and correlate with short bursts of 500/504 responses from the API and unzippered streaming disconnects.

Impact:
- Several user-facing features in AuroraAnalytics' product observed request failures and increased median/ p95/p99 latency for ~2-6 minute windows.
- Customer reports elevated error rates for one-hour periods across the last 3 days, with brief sessions of complete timeouts for some flows.

Environment:
- prod (dedicated) - customer-dc: aurora-prod-usw1
- Affected regions observed: us-west primary, some cross-region fanout to us-east during failover

Initial hypothesis:
- DNS-based egress failover (internal egress-router using short TTL) caused a subset of nodes to resolve to an unintended egress endpoint in a different region, creating a hairpin cross-region path. This added RTT and occasionally triggered client-side timeouts and server-side inference queueing/backpressure.

Next steps planned:
- Capture DNS resolution patterns and TTL changes from edge proxies and egress-router during next window.
- Temporarily pin egress for the customer's dedicated pool to us-west to test mitigation.
- Correlate with load balancer logs, VPC NAT metrics, and GPU queue lengths on serving nodes.
steps_to_reproduce: From a client in us-west, send sustained inference requests to the customer's dedicated endpoint (rate ~50 r/s) for 10 minutes.
Observe DNS answers from internal egress-router and measure time-to-first-byte and full response time per request.
During a simulated DNS reload (short TTL expiration), observe whether some clients are routed to an alternate egress zone (us-east) and whether this increases p99 latency and causes 504s.
Check streaming sockets for premature closes correlated with DNS switch events.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Maya Patel (Support): Customer reported repeated 504s during morning traffic window. Attached customer logs and approximate timestamps. Requested SRE assistance to triage potential routing/egress issues.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Luis Ramirez (SRE): Confirmed elevated p99 and intermittent 5xx spikes in the customer's dedicated pool between 09:40-09:46 UTC. No obvious increase in GPU saturation, but saw transient increases in request queue length on 2 serving nodes.
2026-03-11 14:32 - AuroraAnalytics (Customer): We can provide packet captures and a list of client IPs affected. Issue caused user-facing errors; would like an ETA for mitigation.

2026-03-12 16:20 - Luis Ramirez (SRE): Applied temporary egress pin for aurora-prod-usw1 to force all egress through us-west-1 NATs. Monitoring for recurrence. Asked infra to pull DNS cache logs and TTL churn metrics.
2026-03-13 08:42 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer confirmed reduced errors after pinning, but occasional spikes still observed. Requested deeper DNS resolution trace and egress-router config review.

2026-03-14 11:10 - Network Eng (Anika Bose): Found that internal DNS proxy performed aggressive failover when healthcheck latencies exceeded 120ms; in some cases it selected alternate egress endpoints in us-east causing hairpin. Preparing PR to increase healthcheck hysteresis and to add region-affinity weighting.
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between DNS A/AAAA answer changes from egress-router and ~200-300ms jump in TTFB for affected requests.

GPU utilization on serving nodes stayed between 40-60% during incidents; however, request queue length spiked briefly on nodes that received hairpinned traffic, indicating added network RTT causing backend scheduling jitter.
Load balancer and NAT gateway logs show a small percentage (~0.6%) of connections egressing via us-east during windows where errors appeared.
Healthcheck logs show repeated transient latency spikes from a subset of NAT instances in us-west; the egress-router's failover logic has TTL=15s and immediate switch-on-failure semantics.
No application-level bugs found in model server; traces show request spent extra time in network and in waiting for connection establishment after DNS change.
Slack cross-ref: #support thread <https://slack.redwood.com/support/t/ABC123> and incident channel #inc-19230 in progress.
resolution: 2026-03-12 - Mitigation: Temporarily pinned aurora-prod-usw1 egress to a specific us-west NAT pool to eliminate cross-region resolution. Customer reported immediate reduction in 504s.

Planned fix: Increase egress-router healthcheck hysteresis and add region-affinity weighting to DNS selection to avoid immediate cross-region switch on transient latency. PRs: egress-router PR#412 (pending review) and dns-proxy PR#88 (adds TTL smoothing).

Follow-up actions: Run a 48h canary with modified egress-router settings for dedicated pools, add telemetry for DNS answer churn per-customer, and create automated alert on >0.2% cross-region egress from a dedicated pool.
Postmortem: Drafting a short postmortem and will link once complete. Customer scheduled a sync with customer success for 2026-03-16.
